newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African fund manager discloses record JSE deal.
newsitem.headline: S.African fund manager discloses record JSE deal.

text.p: South African fund manager Southern Asset Management (SAM) said on Monday it had concluded a two billion rand portfolio trade on June 17 -- the largest single trade ever on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
The deal, which was transacted by stockbrokers SBC Warburg, involved the buying and selling of 107 shares as part of the reshaping of its portfolios, Southern said in a statement.
Chief investment officer Avril Stassen said the deal was in line with the introduction of a core and satellite investment style at Southern Asset Management from May 1 this year.
"The transaction with SBC Warburg involving all 107 stocks was concluded in one large trade," Stassen said.
The two billion rand transaction was the equivalent of two day's turnover on the exchange, which averages around 800 million rand a day.
Stassen added that as the deal was completed within one day's JSE trade, the impact on SAM's portfolios was immediate.
"This is of benefit to our policyholders, group clients and shareholders because all our portfolios were involved," he said.
